title: Typhoid fever: extensive intraphagocytic (macrophage) multiplication
vignette: A 42-year-old man comes to the office due to 2 weeks of progressive fever, chills, abdominal discomfort, and loose stools, which began during a trip to Southeast Asia. He received no pretravel vaccinations and did not strictly follow food and water safety precautions during the trip. The patient had an episode of Salmonella Enteritidis gastroenteritis last year, and it resolved with symptomatic care. Temperature is 39.4 C (102.9 F), blood pressure is 110/64 mm Hg, pulse is 62/min, and respirations are 18/min. Physical examination shows a faint macular rash on the trunk. There is mild tenderness to palpation in the lower abdominal quadrants with no guarding or rebound tenderness. Hepatosplenomegaly is present. Blood culture grows gram-negative, non-lactose-fermenting rods. Which of the following pathogenic mechanisms best explains this patient's prolonged and severe disease course compared to his prior episode of bacterial gastroenteritis?

clues.note: An escalating fever over days-to-weeks (rather than an acute self-limited illness) is characteristic of typhoid fever.
Relative bradycardia despite a high fever (pulse-temperature dissociation) is a classic clue to typhoid fever.

clues.text: faint macular rash on the trunk
clues.note: Faint salmon-colored macules on the trunk are 'rose spots,' typical of typhoid fever.
Hepatosplenomegaly reflects systemic spread of the organism through the reticuloendothelial system.
Gram-negative, non-lactose-fermenting rods on blood culture fit Salmonella - here the TYPHOIDAL strain (S. Typhi).

whatMatters: Escalating fever + relative bradycardia + rose spots + hepatosplenomegaly + gram-negative non-lactose-fermenting rods after travel = TYPHOID FEVER (Salmonella Typhi). Typhoidal strains (Vi capsule) evade neutrophils and undergo EXTENSIVE INTRACELLULAR (intraphagocytic) MULTIPLICATION in macrophages, disseminating systemically - explaining the prolonged, severe course. Answer C.
strategy: Contrast NONtyphoidal (his prior self-limited gastroenteritis: neutrophilic inflammation, stays local) with TYPHOIDAL Salmonella (Vi capsule inhibits neutrophil killing -> survives and MULTIPLIES inside macrophages -> spreads via lymphatics/reticuloendothelial system -> systemic typhoid). The severity comes from intracellular replication in phagocytes. Reject contact-dependent cytotoxicity (Entamoeba), cross-reacting antibodies (Campylobacter/Guillain-Barre), and villus destruction (rotavirus/Giardia).

eliminations.label: Contact-dependent host cytotoxicity - Entamoeba histolytica
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: direct contact killing of host cells (e.g., Entamoeba histolytica inserting a pore-forming protein), causing bloody diarrhea/liver abscess. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this patient has typhoid features and gram-negative rods on culture, not amebic contact cytotoxicity. ✅ Correct if: amebic dysentery/liver abscess.

eliminations.label: Cross-reacting antibody formation - Campylobacter/rheumatic
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: antibodies against a pathogen cross-reacting with host tissue (e.g., Campylobacter -> Guillain-Barre via anti-ganglioside antibodies). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: typhoid severity is from intracellular replication, not molecular mimicry; rose spots/relative bradycardia point to S. Typhi. ✅ Correct if: post-Campylobacter Guillain-Barre or rheumatic fever.

eliminations.label: Villus epithelial cell destruction - rotavirus/Giardia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: damage to intestinal villi causing malabsorptive diarrhea (rotavirus, Giardia). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it explains watery diarrhea, not the systemic, prolonged typhoid picture with hepatosplenomegaly and bacteremia. ✅ Correct if: villous-blunting malabsorptive diarrhea.

reasoning: Travel + escalating fever + relative bradycardia + rose spots + hepatosplenomegaly + gram-negative non-lactose-fermenting rods = typhoid fever (S. Typhi)
Typhoidal strains carry the Vi capsule, which inhibits neutrophil recruitment/phagocytosis
They survive and MULTIPLY inside macrophages, spreading via lymphatics and the reticuloendothelial system
mechanism: Salmonella species are gram-negative, non-lactose-fermenting, motile enteric rods split into NONtyphoidal and TYPHOIDAL strains. Both invade intestinal epithelium, but the course then diverges. NONtyphoidal strains (e.g., S. Enteritidis, his prior illness) are phagocytosed by neutrophils/macrophages in the lamina propria and provoke a robust NEUTROPHILIC inflammatory response, producing a usually self-limited gastroenteritis. TYPHOIDAL strains (S. Typhi/Paratyphi) possess the Vi CAPSULAR ANTIGEN and other virulence factors that INHIBIT neutrophil recruitment and phagocytosis and blunt the macrophage oxidative burst - so instead of being killed, the bacteria undergo EXTENSIVE INTRACELLULAR (INTRAPHAGOCYTIC) MULTIPLICATION within macrophages and disseminate through the lymphatics and RETICULOENDOTHELIAL SYSTEM. This produces typhoid fever: escalating fever with relative bradycardia (pulse-temperature dissociation), rose spots, hepatosplenomegaly, abdominal pain, and (later) GI bleeding/perforation. Blood culture is diagnostic. The prolonged, severe, systemic course - versus his prior self-limited gastroenteritis - is explained by this intracellular replication in phagocytes.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro > typhoidal Salmonella (S. Typhi): Vi capsule inhibits phagocytosis/neutrophils, extensive intracellular replication in macrophages -> systemic typhoid (rose spots, relative bradycardia, hepatosplenomegaly); nontyphoidal = neutrophilic gastroenteritis.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Typhoid severity = survival + multiplication inside macrophages (intraphagocytic), spreading via reticuloendothelial system.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on typhoidal vs nontyphoidal Salmonella, Vi capsule, reticuloendothelial system, rose spots, or pulse-temperature dissociation? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Contact cytotoxicity = Entamoeba; cross-reacting antibodies = Campylobacter/rheumatic; villus destruction = rotavirus/Giardia.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: S. Typhi = Vi capsule + intracellular replication in macrophages -> typhoid fever (rose spots, relative bradycardia, HSM).

keywords.front: Escalating fever + relative bradycardia + rose spots + hepatosplenomegaly (travel)

keywords.back: Vi capsule -> intracellular (intraphagocytic) multiplication in macrophages
Nontyphoidal = neutrophilic gastroenteritis; typhoidal = systemic typhoid
Relative bradycardia with high fever (typhoid, also others)
Inhibits neutrophil recruitment/phagocytosis and oxidative burst

firstAid.detail: Micro: S. Typhi Vi capsule -> intracellular replication in macrophages -> systemic disease.
Micro > Entamoeba (contact cytotoxicity), Campylobacter (cross-reacting Ab), rotavirus/Giardia (villus).
Micro > rose spots, relative bradycardia, hepatosplenomegaly; GI bleed/perforation late.

memoryHook: Typhoid Salmonella hides inside macrophages and multiplies there (Vi capsule cloaks it from neutrophils), riding the reticuloendothelial system to a slow, systemic fever with rose spots.
